newsitem.title: USA: Sumitomo Bank Calif. denies racial bias.
newsitem.headline: Sumitomo Bank Calif. denies racial bias.

text.p: Sumitomo Bank of California on Tuesday denied allegations of racial discrimination in its employment practices.
The bank was responding to a complaint filed Monday with the U.S. Labor Department by a coalition of minority groups led by the Greenlining Institute.
The bank, owned by Sumitomo Bank Ltd, said in a statement that the charges were made "on the basis of inaccurate, misleading and distorted claims."
"We take this opportunity to respond to what we feel is a carefully orchestrated media campaign seeking to unnecessarily inflame and incite the public," it said.

The complaint said, "Sumitomo's minority and women employment record at the management and professional level is the worst of any bank in California and is likely to be the worst for any major bank in the United States."

The complaint was filed with the Labor Department's Office of Federal Contract Compliance, which investigates possible violations of civil rights law covering employment discrimination by companies receiving federal contract money.

Sumitomo said that over the last four years it has "aggressively pursued" a policy to meet the requirements of a 1977 law designed to ensure that banks lend to people in their local communities, including low-income neighborhoods.

It also said 18.8 percent of its managers, assistant vice presidents and higher, are non-Japanese Asian-Americans. Managers include African-Americans, Hispanics, Korean-Americans, Filipino-Americans and a Vietnamese-American, it said.
The bank said it "does not tolerate discriminatory behavior and has not created a hostile environment" for women and minorities.
